paper_title: VideoLLaMB Long-context Video Understanding with Recurrent Memory   Bridges
caption: GPU Memory Cost. We apply all the experiments on a single NVIDIA A800 GPU.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the memory usage of five different models as the number of frames increases. The x-axis is labeled "Number of Frames" and employs a linear scale ranging from 0 to slightly beyond 1000, with numeric tick marks spaced at regular intervals of 200. The y-axis is labeled "Memory (GB)" and uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to roughly 425, with tick marks spaced at intervals of 50. The line for VideoLLaMB is a solid pink line with circular markers, though it is almost completely obscured by the visually identical trajectory of the VideoLLaMB-R line. The VideoLLaMB-R line is a solid olive-gold line with circular markers, starting at approximately 18 GB at near zero frames and rising very gradually to roughly 38 GB at the final data point just past 1000 frames. The line for PLLaVA is a solid green line with circular markers, starting near 18 GB and showing a steady, moderate increase to approximately 75 GB at the end of the x-axis. The line for LLaVA-NeXT is a solid blue line with circular markers, beginning near 18 GB and increasing steadily across the chart, ending at approximately 145 GB. Finally, the line for VideoLLaVA is a solid purple line with circular markers that starts near 18 GB and exhibits a steep, rapid increase; it records values of roughly 120 GB near 125 frames and 230 GB near 250 frames, before continuing sharply upward and exiting the top boundary of the plot prior to the 400-frame mark.
